summary: The deadband keeps 0.5 (the audit's option 2) and geom.c:561-598 now states the missing hypothesis at the point of derivation: surface_scale_factor == 1, the two coordinate spaces named, geom_line_params() cited for the geometry stage working in guest pixels, the quarter-of-a-guest-pixel figure at Rendering Scale 2 stated, the one-directional argument given, and the cost measured by a new instrument rather than described. NOTES.md:292-300 marks the original paragraph corrected IN PLACE, above the text it corrects. The rejected option's price is real: lineParams' four components are all live (geom.c:235-239), vertex_push_offset = GEOM_PUSH_CONSTANT_SIZE (shaders.c:841) puts a vec4 array at offset 16 (vsh.c:994-999) so the range grows 16 -> 32 and not 16 -> 20, and shaders.c:44-50, 317-327 declares it on every graphics pipeline layout for descriptor-set compatibility.
scenario: Pass 2b's scenario -- a reader at Rendering Scale 2 told by the comment that the deadband provably removes no sample, while it silently suppresses 191 clips such a device would have sampled -- can no longer occur: the comment now says at which scale the proof holds, that it is conservative above it, and what that costs (191/278/112 at scale 2, 295/860/298 at 3, 337/1666/568 at 4). line_cap_phase.py --scale-cost reproduces that table here exactly, its scale-1 control reads zero on every column, and its non-trivial leg -- every over-reached sample must be one covers() agrees the shipped footprint lights -- reports FAIL on 57 phantom samples under a sample-index-off-by-half mutant run from a symlink copy. The scale-independence claim reproduces exactly (first cut Line_0024.0, 19 captures cut, at all of scales 1-4). The commit is comment-only by two independent checks: a C-comment strip of geom.c at 4cc0d26dc0 and at 68b5ac7dcb is identical, and geom_dump built against both trees emits byte-identical GLSL, md5 d16bf20f526caf274e5f58640b72823d, so b_ref 36e85c96c9 is still the last commit on this branch that can move a pixel.
evidence: hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/glsl/geom.c:546-598 (the derivation and the stated hypothesis), :829-838 (scale-independence), :235-239 (lineParams); docs/lanes/linecap13/NOTES.md:292-300, 353-440; docs/testing/line_cap_phase.py scale_cost()/over_reach()/covers(); hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/shaders.c:44-60, 317-330, 841; hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/glsl/vsh.c:985-1005; hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/vk/draw.c:1204-1212, 2756-2786.

summary: LEG C2 keeps Line_width/Fill_* under must_not_move on the premise that, with widen_lines false, the generator emits the byte-identical shader it emitted before and so nothing in this branch's diff can reach those captures. The arm on a_ref 28a3805b93 / b_ref 36e85c96c9, 2 runs per side, violated exactly that leg (Fill_0032.0 26721 -> 26717) and ab_compare classed it ATTRIBUTABLE to the change. Reading the capture files rather than the scores: the change moves 4 px of Fill_0032.0 (6 px on the pre-deadband arm) and EVERY ONE of them moves to the golden's exact value, including one going from lit cyan (54,252,252) to the golden's background (32,34,36) -- the cap clip's own signature. Fill_0000.0 and Fill_0001.0, both narrow, do not move at all, which is what the deadband predicts. The goldens themselves are width-dependent for this test: Fill_0032.0 differs from Fill_0000.0 in 12,021 px. The widened-line path is reached by this capture and the premise is false.
scenario: As registered the prediction cannot pass. The arms job runs every registered prediction whose refs are live, so any re-registration that keeps Line_width/Fill_* under must_not_move fails on Fill_0032.0 again the moment the change works; arms.sh recomputes the regressed label from the verdicts and fold.sh:503-510 refuses to fold a regressed PR, so the lane is parked on a leg that fires on success. Independently of the fold: the PR body, NOTES.md and the prediction all tell the next reader that a capture nothing in the diff can reach moved anyway, so the next genuine Fill_* regression will be read as the same unexplained device noise. Nondeterminism is excluded three ways -- 2 runs per arm each byte-identical with itself, the two arms' base captures pixel-identical across all three base runs, and the two fix captures differing from each other by exactly the 2 px the deadband accounts for.
remediation: Name what actually draws in Line_width/Fill_0032.0 -- the evidence says the widened-line path runs for it, so widen_lines is not false there and the byte-identical-fill-shader argument does not apply. Then re-scope C2 before the next arm: Fill_0000.*/Fill_0001.* stay in must_not_move, Fill_0032.0 moves to the improving side. This is a post-hoc edit to a leg that fired, which this lane has twice been right to resist; what makes it legitimate here is that the device falsified the PREMISE and not the result. Say so in the file, and re-register -- nothing else clears the regressed label.
evidence: docs/testing/predictions/line-cap-clip.json:15 and the Fill_* stanza of LEG C2 in the prediction text; the PR body's 'One thing this lane cannot settle'; docs/lanes/linecap13/NOTES.md:344; arms/pairs/82cbbed7e047....verdict.txt (must not move, but moved: Line_width/Fill_0032.0 26721 -> 26717; 20 better, 0 worse, 146 same); dispatch/results/1789866964-arms-linecap13-base-2557022 and -fix-2557051 captures1+captures2, dispatch/results/1789834717-arms-linecap13-base-3127464 and -fix-3127486 captures1, against goldens/results/Line_width/Fill_*.png.

summary: 'It gives up nothing at scale 1' (NOTES.md:406) and geom.c:595-596's control row are measured over the 48 non-void Line_* captures, which is the only set any instrument in this lane scores. On the device at surface_scale_factor 1 the deadband gives up 2 px of Fill_0032.0 that the pre-deadband build got exactly right: (271,93) 51,154,152 -> 51,155,151 and (264,123) 51,227,79 -> 51,228,78, with the golden at the pre-deadband value in both. Both arms' base captures of that capture are pixel-identical, so the difference is the deadband and not the master commits merged between the arms. These are shaded VALUES and not coverage flips: the half-pixel proof bounds which samples are inside the footprint, but taking a cut also synthesises a vertex and re-triangulates the strip, changing how the varyings interpolate at samples that stay covered.
scenario: A later reader -- in particular the next lane on #13's colour phase, which is 76.3% of the issue's residual -- takes 'exact at scale 1' and 'gives up nothing at scale 1' at face value and sizes the deadband's cost at zero for the configuration every arm and every golden in this campaign runs at (desktop_channel.sh pins surface_scale = 1). The true cost is small but non-zero, it lands in the colour channel that lane is about, and no instrument in this repository reports it: --rivals, --controls, --shader, --quantise and --scale-cost all score ink masks or sample coverage, and --depth is value-aware only for z.
remediation: Documentation, not code: say that the half-pixel proof bounds COVERAGE and not interpolated values; scope the scale-1 'costs nothing' claim to the 48 Line_* captures the instruments score; and record the two pixels, since they are the only measurement of the deadband's true cost at scale 1 that exists. Whether to chase the value class needs a device and is a separate decision.
evidence: docs/lanes/linecap13/NOTES.md:404-408; hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/glsl/geom.c:573-598; dispatch/results/1789834717-arms-linecap13-fix-3127486/captures1 against 1789866965-arms-linecap13-fix-2557051/captures1 and captures2 on Line_width::Fill_0032.0.png (2 px differ), both against goldens/results/Line_width/Fill_0032.0.png; the base captures of both arms are identical.

summary: The PR body says: against the 393 guest px the cap rule removes at scale 1 (--controls), the deadband gives up on the order of a twelfth of the clip's own work above 1x. geom.c:592-597 and NOTES.md:404-406 both carry the conversion that makes a twelfth true ('scaled for comparison', 'whose device-sample equivalent scales with scale^2'); the PR body and the commit message of 68b5ac7dcb drop it. Read with the numbers in the paragraph above it, 112 against 393 is about 28%, four times the stated figure.
scenario: A reader quoting the PR body -- which is what the board and the next lane read first -- computes the deadband's cost as a quarter of the cap rule's work rather than a twelfth, from two numbers in different units: device samples at scale 2 against guest pixels at scale 1. Two of this campaign's standing lessons are this exact shape.
remediation: Add the scale^2 conversion to the PR body's sentence, as geom.c and NOTES.md already have it.
evidence: PR #141 body, the 'Pass-2b audit A1 (MEDIUM) remediated' section; hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/glsl/geom.c:592-597; docs/lanes/linecap13/NOTES.md:404-406; the commit message of 68b5ac7dcb.
